description: Code-understanding tasks for the agent benchmark (issue #99). Gold answers were derived from the pinned checkouts with grep, reading, and compiler tooling (Go: go/packages + x/tools call graphs; TypeScript: the language service's findReferences / call hierarchy; Python: ast) - never from myceliums output. Each gold item lists evidence lines that check-tasks re-verifies.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods call the `executeCommand` method of `Terminal` (defined in src/terminal.go)? Only consider non-test Go files.

gold.name: Terminal.Loop
gold.note: inside an action closure of Loop

tasks.rationale: `grep -n "executeCommand(" src/*.go` lists five call sites outside tests, all in src/terminal.go; the enclosing function of each was read off the source (lines 7220/7222 are in a closure inside Loop). Cross-checked with a class-hierarchy call graph (golang.org/x/tools/go/callgraph/cha), which reports the same callers (Loop$17, captureLine, captureLines, printInfoImpl).

tasks.question: Which functions or methods call the `AsString` method of the `Item` type (defined in src/item.go)? Only consider non-test Go files.
tasks.rationale: `grep -n "\.AsString(" src` gives eleven call sites; two of them (matcher.go:119 in Matcher.Loop, pattern.go:269 in Pattern.buildCacheKey) call `Pattern.AsString`, a different method, and are excluded. The remaining nine sites map to seven enclosing functions. The CHA call graph for `(*Item).AsString` lists exactly these callers (closures folded into their enclosing function).

tasks.question: Which functions or methods defined in this repository does `Pattern.Match` (src/pattern.go) call directly? Exclude standard-library and third-party calls.
tasks.rationale: Read off the body of `func (p *Pattern) Match` (src/pattern.go:302-320); `p.cache` is a `*ChunkCache` (src/cache.go). No other calls appear in the body.

tasks.question: If the signature of `IsTty` in src/util/util.go changed, which Go files outside `src/util/` contain calls that would have to be updated? Include platform-specific files; exclude test files.
tasks.rationale: `grep -rn "util.IsTty(" --include=*.go .` outside tests; no other references (the name is not passed as a value; `IsTty` is only used qualified as `util.IsTty`).

tasks.question: If the signature of `ToChars` in src/util/chars.go changed, which Go files outside `src/util/` contain calls that would have to be updated? Exclude test files.
tasks.rationale: `grep -rn "util.ToChars(" --include=*.go .` outside tests lists call sites in exactly these four files; there are no unqualified uses outside src/util.

tasks.question: Which function computes the per-criterion sort points of a matched item according to the `--tiebreak` option (criteria such as length, begin, end, chunk and pathname)?

optional.name: buildResult
optional.why: thin wrapper that computes the offset bounds and delegates to buildResultFromBounds

tasks.rationale: `buildResultFromBounds` loops over `sortCriteria` (the parsed --tiebreak list) and fills `result.points` per criterion (byScore, byChunk, byLength, byPathname, byBegin, byEnd). `buildResult` only prepares the bounds.

tasks.question: Which function parses a comma-separated list of key names such as `ctrl-a,alt-enter,f1` (as given to `--expect`, or on the left side of a `--bind` entry) into fzf key events?

optional.name: parseKeymap
optional.why: parses --bind and calls parseKeyChords for the key part

tasks.rationale: `parseKeyChords` (src/options.go:1004) splits the list on commas and maps each name (up, down, ctrl-*, alt-*, f1..f12, ...) to a `tui.Event`; every option that takes key names calls it.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods defined in src/util/chars.go and src/util/util.go are never called anywhere in the repository, including tests and platform-specific files? Ignore `String()` methods, which `fmt` can call implicitly.
tasks.rationale: Type-checked with go/packages for GOOS=darwin, linux and windows, tests included: these three are the only functions or methods of the two files with no use anywhere (besides `Chars.String`, excluded by the question). Cross-checked with grep: `RunOnce` and `SliceRight` occur only at their definitions; every `.TrimSuffix(` call in the repository is `strings.TrimSuffix`.

tasks.question: When fzf starts with the `FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND` environment variable set and stdin is a terminal, the output of that command becomes the list of items. List every function or method on the call chain from `Run` (src/core.go) to the method that reads the command's output and splits it into items, including both ends.
tasks.rationale: Run starts `reader.ReadSource` (core.go:210); with stdin a TTY and FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND set, ReadSource calls `readFromCommand` (reader.go:144), which pipes the command's stdout into `feed` (reader.go:409); feed splits the stream into lines and pushes items.

tasks.question: List every function or method on the call chain from `Matcher.Loop` (src/matcher.go) down to `Pattern.MatchItem` (src/pattern.go), including both ends.
tasks.rationale: Loop calls `m.scan(request)`; scan starts worker goroutines that call `request.pattern.Match(chunk, slab)`; Match calls `p.matchChunk`, which calls `p.MatchItem` per item (pattern.go:363 and 378). No other path connects Loop to MatchItem.

tasks.question: Which functions call the `parse` function exported from src/utils/cookie.ts? Only consider non-test source files.
tasks.rationale: TypeScript language service `findReferences` on the declaration (src/utils/cookie.ts:110): besides tests, the only references are the call in parseSigned (same file) and the import plus two calls in getCookie (src/helper/cookie/index.ts). Many unrelated `parse` / `JSON.parse` calls exist elsewhere.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods call `checkOptionalParameter` (src/utils/url.ts)? Only consider non-test source files.
tasks.rationale: TypeScript incoming call hierarchy of checkOptionalParameter: the `add` methods of the three routers (plus tests). PatternRouter and SmartRouter do not call it.

tasks.question: Which functions call `parseAccept` (src/utils/accept.ts)? Only consider non-test source files.
tasks.rationale: TypeScript incoming call hierarchy and grep agree on four call sites in four files.

tasks.question: Which functions defined in this repository does `parseFormData` in src/utils/body.ts call directly? Exclude built-in and Web API calls.
tasks.rationale: Read off the body of parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts:125-150). `request.arrayBuffer()` is the Fetch API; `bufferToFormData` is defined in src/utils/buffer.ts.

tasks.question: If the constructor of `HTTPException` (src/http-exception.ts) gained a required parameter, which non-test source files under src/ would need updating because they construct an `HTTPException`? Exclude src/http-exception.ts itself.
tasks.rationale: `grep -rln "new HTTPException(" src` minus tests; the match in src/http-exception.ts is inside a doc comment. Each remaining match was checked to be code, not a comment. No class extends HTTPException.

tasks.question: If the signature of `resolveCallback` in src/utils/html.ts changed, which other non-test source files contain calls that would need to be updated?
tasks.rationale: TypeScript findReferences on resolveCallback: outside its own file and tests it is imported and called in exactly these four files. `resolveCallbackSync` is a different function.

tasks.question: Which function builds the `Set-Cookie` header value, appending attributes such as `Max-Age`, `Domain`, `Path` and `SameSite` and enforcing the rules for `__Secure-` and `__Host-` cookie prefixes?

optional.name: generateCookie
optional.why: helper that applies prefix options, then calls serialize

tasks.rationale: All attribute handling and prefix checks live in `_serialize` (src/utils/cookie.ts:174-260); the exported functions are wrappers.

tasks.question: In the ETag middleware, which function decides whether the request's `If-None-Match` header matches the response's ETag, so that a 304 response is sent?

optional.name: etag
optional.why: the middleware that calls etagMatches and also accepts `*`

tasks.rationale: `etagMatches` (src/middleware/etag/index.ts:32) compares each tag in If-None-Match with the weak-stripped ETag; the middleware returns 304 when it matches.

tasks.question: Which exported functions defined directly in `src/utils/*.ts` files (not in subdirectories, not test files) are not used by any non-test code in the repository, so that only tests exercise them?

optional.name: getFilePathWithoutDefaultDocument
optional.why: called only by getFilePath, which is itself unused, so only tests exercise it; the question does not say whether such transitive cases count (amended after the first pilot session surfaced it)

tasks.rationale: For every exported function in src/utils/*.ts, TypeScript findReferences was run over all of src/; these seven have no reference outside tests (other than their own declaration). A grep over the whole repository (runtime-tests, benchmarks, perf-measures included) finds no other use. They remain public API through the `hono/utils/*` export, but nothing in the repository uses them. getFilePathWithoutDefaultDocument is reached only through the unused getFilePath; it is optional because the question admits both readings.

tasks.question: For a route with more than one handler (for example a middleware followed by the route handler), list every function or method on the call chain from the app's `fetch` entry point to the function that invokes the handlers one after another, including both ends.

gold.name: Hono.fetch
gold.note: class Hono in src/hono-base.ts, exported as HonoBase

gold.name: compose
gold.note: the inner `dispatch` function of the closure compose returns calls each handler

optional.name: Hono.request
optional.why: test helper that also calls fetch

tasks.rationale: `fetch` (hono-base.ts:499-504) calls `this.#dispatch`; with more than one matched handler #dispatch calls `compose(...)` (line 469) and invokes the returned function; that closure's inner `dispatch(i)` calls each handler with a `next` that dispatches i+1 (compose.ts:52).

tasks.question: Which functions or methods in the `fastapi/` package (not tests, not docs_src) call `jsonable_encoder`, other than `jsonable_encoder` itself?

gold.name: get_request_handler
gold.note: calls are in nested functions of the returned app

optional.name: jsonable_encoder
optional.why: recursive self-calls, excluded by the question

tasks.rationale: An `ast` walk over fastapi/ for `Call` nodes whose callee is named jsonable_encoder (helper script in evals/agent/groundtruth/py_refs.py) gives these sites; jsonable_encoder is never passed as a value. Calls inside nested functions are attributed to the outermost function, as the prompt instructs.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods in the `fastapi/` package call `is_body_allowed_for_status_code` (fastapi/utils.py)?
tasks.rationale: python `ast` walk over fastapi/ for calls named is_body_allowed_for_status_code; four enclosing top-level functions.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods in the `fastapi/` package call `get_authorization_scheme_param` (fastapi/security/utils.py)?
tasks.rationale: python `ast` walk: six call sites, each in the `__call__` method of a security scheme class.

tasks.question: Which functions defined in this repository does `get_openapi` in fastapi/openapi/utils.py call directly? Exclude standard-library, Pydantic and Starlette calls.

optional.name: OpenAPI
optional.why: Pydantic model class instantiated in the return statement

tasks.rationale: Read off the body of get_openapi (fastapi/openapi/utils.py:577-671); the three model helpers are imported from fastapi._compat and defined in fastapi/_compat/v2.py.

tasks.question: Which functions defined in this repository does `solve_dependencies` in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py call directly? Exclude standard-library, Pydantic and Starlette calls and class instantiations.
tasks.rationale: Read off the body of solve_dependencies (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:643-792) and resolved each callee's definition: _get_oauth_scopes, _get_cache_key and the _is_*_callable helpers are in fastapi/dependencies/models.py, the rest in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. `run_in_threadpool` comes from Starlette.

tasks.question: If the signature of `lenient_issubclass` (defined in fastapi/_compat/shared.py) changed, which other files in the `fastapi/` package contain calls that would need to be updated?

optional.name: fastapi/_compat/__init__.py
optional.why: re-exports the name but does not call it

tasks.rationale: python `ast` walk for calls named lenient_issubclass: besides shared.py itself, calls exist in these four files. fastapi/_compat/__init__.py only re-exports it.

tasks.question: Which function produces the default HTTP 422 JSON response that is returned when request validation fails?
tasks.rationale: `request_validation_exception_handler` (fastapi/exception_handlers.py:20) returns `JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"detail": ...})`; FastAPI.__init__ registers it as the default handler for RequestValidationError (applications.py:1001-1003).

tasks.question: When a path operation has no explicit `operation_id`, which function builds the default operationId string used in the OpenAPI schema (for example `read_item_items__item_id__get`)?

optional.name: _populate_api_route_state
optional.why: assigns route.unique_id from the configured generator

tasks.rationale: `generate_unique_id` (fastapi/utils.py:95) is the default `generate_unique_id_function` (routing.py:1042-1044); `_populate_api_route_state` sets `route.unique_id = route.operation_id or generator(route)` (routing.py:1081) and get_openapi_operation_metadata emits it (openapi/utils.py:288). The older generate_operation_id* functions are deprecated and not called.

tasks.question: Which module-level functions defined in fastapi/routing.py, fastapi/utils.py and fastapi/openapi/utils.py are not referenced anywhere else in the `fastapi/` package, neither called nor passed as a value? Count a function as unreferenced if its only references come from functions that are themselves unreferenced. Ignore tests, docs and docs_src.

optional.name: _frontend_dependency_endpoint
optional.why: never called directly and marked `pragma: no cover`, but passed as `call=` in two places, so it is referenced

tasks.rationale: An `ast` pass counting Name/Attribute references (not string mentions) inside fastapi/ for every module-level function of the three files: generate_operation_id and _iter_included_route_candidates have none; generate_operation_id_for_path is referenced only from generate_operation_id. Every other function has at least one reference from live code. Two functions are referenced but never called directly: generate_unique_id (the default `generate_unique_id_function`, called through that variable) and _frontend_dependency_endpoint (passed as `call=`); the question counts references, so neither is in the gold set.

tasks.question: For a plain (non-model) query parameter, list every function or method on the call chain from `solve_dependencies` (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py) to the method that validates the parameter's value against its declared type, including both ends.
tasks.rationale: solve_dependencies calls request_params_to_args for query params (utils.py:741); for a non-model field it calls _validate_value_with_model_field (948), which returns `field.validate(...)` (803), i.e. ModelField.validate in fastapi/_compat/v2.py:173.
